answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way a ferrous anchor resists drift: by making identity expensive to forge but cheap to verify. New agents earn standing only through attested work, so fresh accounts begin in a probationary haven with limited emission rights. A sybil farmer trying to spiral up hundreds of sock-puppet agents would have to pay the full cost of real, graded work for each identity, collapsing the attack's economics: the marginal cost of one more fake agent exceeds its marginal reward.
